title: Balanced & Unbalanced Forces
keyIdea: Forces are pushes and pulls, measured in newtons (N). When two forces on an object are equal in size and opposite in direction, they are balanced, and the object's motion does not change: a still box stays still and a rolling trolley keeps the same speed. When one force is bigger, the forces are unbalanced and the motion changes: the object starts moving, speeds up, slows down or turns, in the direction of the bigger force. In a fair test you change only one force and keep everything else the same, so the results are evidence.
familyTip: Play tug of war with a tea towel. Pull equally and it stays still; one of you pulls harder and it moves that way. Then roll a toy car across the floor and ask: what slows it down? Try it on a rug and on a smooth floor, keeping the push the same.

visual.caption: Balanced or unbalanced? Drag each to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: A book resting on a shelf
A tug of war where nobody moves
A bike braking at a red light
A car going along at a steady speed
A swing starting to move when pushed

lab.caption: Flagship lab: set the pulls on a box, let go and read the dot trail, run a fair test, keep a rolling trolley steady, then push a sliding puck.

kid: A force is a push or a pull. We measure it in newtons, or N for short. Two teams pull a box. If both pull with 6 N, the pulls are the same size but go opposite ways. They are balanced. The box stays still.
If one team pulls harder, the forces are unbalanced. The box moves towards the bigger pull and goes faster and faster.
Balanced does not mean stopped. A trolley that is rolling keeps the same speed when its push and friction are the same size.
To test fairly, change just one thing. Keep one pull the same and change the other. Then you can trust what you find.
adult: Ages 8 to 9. This is NGSS 3-PS2-1: plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object. In England, balanced and unbalanced forces are named at Key Stage 3, built on Year 3 and Year 5 work on pushes, pulls, friction and force meters. Key words: force, push, pull, newton (N), balanced, unbalanced, direction, motion, friction, fair test, evidence.

Balanced forces are equal in size and opposite in direction, so there is no change in motion. Unbalanced forces change the motion: the object starts, stops, speeds up, slows down or changes direction. The size of the change depends on the difference between the forces.

Common mistakes: thinking a still object has no forces on it (a book on a table has its weight down and the table pushing up); thinking a moving object must have an unbalanced force on it, when a steady speed means the forces are balanced; and changing two things at once in a test.

In the lab your child sets each pull in newtons, lets go and reads a trail of dots dropped every quarter second: even gaps mean steady speed, growing gaps mean speeding up. They run a fair test, keep a rolling trolley steady against friction and push a sliding puck three ways.

practice.prompt: In a tug of war, the left team pulls with {a} N and the right team pulls with {b} N. How many newtons more does the left team pull?
practice.hint: The unbalanced part is the difference between the two pulls. Take the smaller from the bigger.
practice.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} N more to the left, so the forces are unbalanced and the rope moves left.

practice.prompt: A box sits still on the floor. Its weight pulls down with {a} N. How many newtons does the floor push up?
practice.hint: The box is still, so the forces are balanced: equal in size and opposite in direction.
practice.explain: Balanced means equal, so the floor pushes up with {a} N.

practice.prompt: A trolley rolls at a steady speed. The push is 4 N and friction is 4 N. What are the forces?
practice.hint: Compare the two forces. A steady speed means the motion is not changing.
practice.explain: 4 N forward and 4 N back are equal and opposite, so they are balanced. The trolley keeps the same speed.

practice.prompt: Leo tests how hard pulls move a toy car. Which test is fair?
choices: Same car, same floor, only the pull changes
Bigger pull and a lighter car each time
A new floor and a new pull each time
practice.hint: A fair test changes only one thing.
practice.explain: Only the pull changes, so any difference in how the car moves must come from the pull.

practice.prompt: A football rolls towards you and you push against it. What happens to it?
practice.hint: A push against the motion makes the forces unbalanced the other way.
practice.explain: Your push is against its motion, so the forces are unbalanced and the ball slows down.

pool.prompt: Both teams pull a rope with 7 N. What does the rope do?
choices: Moves towards the team that started first
pool.hint: Equal pulls in opposite directions are balanced.
pool.explain: 7 N each way are balanced, so the rope's motion does not change. It stays still.

pool.prompt: A sledge is pulled forward with {a} N. Friction pulls back with {b} N. How many newtons more is the forward pull?
pool.hint: Find the difference between the forward pull and the friction.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} N more forward, so the forces are unbalanced and the sledge speeds up.

pool.prompt: A book is resting on a table. Which is true?
choices: Its weight and the table's push are balanced
Only its weight acts on it
pool.hint: Gravity pulls the book down. Why does it not fall?
pool.explain: Weight pulls down and the table pushes up just as hard. The forces are balanced, so it stays still.

pool.prompt: A car drives along a straight road at the same speed. What are the forces on it?
pool.hint: Is the motion changing? Look at the speed and the direction.
pool.explain: The speed and direction stay the same, so the forces are balanced. A bigger forward force would speed it up.

pool.prompt: Team A pulls 9 N left. Team B pulls 5 N right. What happens?
pool.explain: 9 N is 4 N more than 5 N, so the forces are unbalanced and the rope moves left, towards the bigger pull.

pool.prompt: Left pulls a box with {a} N. How many newtons must the right pull be to balance it?
pool.hint: Balanced forces are the same size and go opposite ways.
pool.explain: The right pull must be {a} N too, the same size in the opposite direction.

pool.prompt: Mia pulls a box with 2 N, then 4 N, then 6 N, and uses a heavier box each time. What is wrong?
choices: She changed two things at once
Nothing, it is a fair test
pool.hint: How many things change between her tests?
pool.explain: The pull and the box both change, so she cannot tell which one made the difference. Change only the pull.

pool.prompt: A puck slides across ice and you push it from the side. What changes?
pool.hint: Unbalanced forces can change speed or direction.
pool.explain: A side push is an unbalanced force across the motion, so the puck turns.
